comment: The gateway's wire contract, minus everything upstream publishes. The signed payload families — the connect pair (funduq-connect-provider / funduq-connect-funduq), kyok-call, cancel, view, resolve, the actor-chain form — and the two delivery envelopes (delivered-run, delivered-completion, model_dump(by_alias=True)) are vectored in docs/upstream-contract-vectors.json, vendored verbatim from upstream funduq's docs/contract-vectors.json at contract revision 21. What moved at revision 18: everything funduq itself puts in a caller's bag now sits one level down under forwardedProps.funduq ({kyok, actorChain, addressedRunId}), and every key it writes into A2A metadata sits under metadata.funduq — so a caller's own keys and funduq's can never collide. Revision 19 deleted the 'input-required' run status: a run that finished asking is 'completed', what it is waiting on is read from its events (funduq.pause.open_asks), an answer is a NEW run naming its parentRunId, and an A2A task is that lineage — task id = root run id, state = tail run's — which is also the id a resolve proof is signed over. Revision 21 made reading one surface (Funduq.as_reader(key)) and refuses a chain presented at a door that cannot say who presented it, which is what presenter_proof below is for. The funduq-delegate family is GONE — the session delegation certificate was removed at revision 15 and nothing here signs, sends or relays one. What remains this file's to state: the wire version, this gateway's own presenter proof, and each socket's frame vocabulary. All three in-repo implementations' suites (gateway, souk-agent-sdk, souk-client-sdk) plus the Go pod-probe consume this file; the inbound frame sets are the module constants the gateway's dispatch reads, asserted equal in tests.

presenter_proof.comment: This gateway's own proof of who is presenting an HTTP request, and the ONLY payload family in this repo that upstream does not define. Contract revision 21 refuses a chain at a door that cannot name its presenter (funduq.errors.PresenterRequired), and funduq_contract publishes six payload builders, none of which authenticates a write — view_payload binds one run_id and so cannot cover a request that opens a run that does not exist yet. Hence a domain tag of OUR own: 'funduq-server-presenter', never 'funduq-presenter', because the funduq-* namespace is upstream's and a name that looks canonical and is not is exactly what the contract vectors exist to prevent. Filed upstream; when a canonical presenter_payload ships, this family is deleted rather than kept beside it. SCOPE: only a caller that presents an actorChain needs it — no chain, no header, no change. A missing, malformed, stale or forged header yields NO key, never an error: core then refuses the chain itself, and one refusal in one place beats two that can disagree. A header that verifies but is not the chain's last hop is core's InvalidChain, not the transport's to pre-empt.
presenter_proof.value_encoding: compact JSON (separators ',' and ':'), the same three fields as every other proof in this system
presenter_proof.payload_notes: UTF-8 bytes; timestamp is whole seconds since the epoch, decimal, no padding; sha256hex is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the EXACT request body bytes sent (sign what you send, not a re-serialization of it). The body hash binds the proof to this one request, so a captured header cannot be replayed onto a different call; the timestamp bounds replay of the same request; the public key inside the payload means the proof names the key it claims.
presenter_proof.freshness_note: funduq.identity.SIGNATURE_FRESHNESS_WINDOW_SECONDS, the same window the cancel and view families use — one window in this system, not two.
presenter_proof.signature: Ed25519 over the payload, hex-encoded, by the same identity that signed the chain's last hop

refusals.chain with no provable presenter: 401 (funduq.errors.PresenterRequired — upstream: "map it to authentication required, not bad request"); on the A2A door only on the v1.0 path, since a2a-sdk's v0.3 compatibility adapter converts every exception into a JSON-RPC internal error inside a 200
refusals.read with no provable presenter: absence — a bound run answers as if it does not exist, never a status

handshake.comment: Two frames. The provider fetches {ticket, funduqPublicKey} from POST /tickets out of band, computes proof = sign(provider_connect_payload(funduqPublicKey, ticket, nonce)) BEFORE connecting, and opens with hello; funduq answers welcome, whose 'answer' is its signature over funduq_connect_payload(ticket, nonce) — the provider verifies it against the pinned key (confirm_connect / WrongFunduq) before treating the link as open. Refusals close 1008 with a reason; 1011 is reserved for server faults. The /ws/kyok hello carries no maxConcurrentRuns. Attach is NAMELESS: nothing is served until a register frame on the open link.

frames.comment: Frame types per socket, after the two-frame handshake. A run frame is {'type': 'run', **DeliveredRun} — dumped by_alias=True and NEVER exclude_none, because RunAgentInput has required fields that are legitimately null ('state', 'forwardedProps') and stripping them makes a good run come back as a permanent refusal; a completion request is {'type': 'completionRequest', 'requestId', **DeliveredCompletion} (actorChain included since contract revision 7), whose 'body' is validated as OpenAI's own chat-completion request shape — 'model' among the required fields — with extension keys allowed through verbatim, and a body that is not one is a 400 before the socket is touched. The ack is three-valued: accepted true, false (transient decline — the run stays queued), or false with a 'reason' (permanent refusal); an ack arriving after funduq's delivery window matches nothing and is simply dropped, which is a guard and not a path. Registration frames are unsigned — the link is the credential: register carries the FULL roster (a smaller batch withdraws omitted names), 'registered' echoes what is now live, deleteAgent/deleteModel remove one record ('deleted' confirms; a refusal — e.g. an agent with a conversation behind it — is answered with an 'error' frame and the socket stays open). The one query is thread_messages — still this wire's, though revision 21 removed it from the FunduqLink ABC: core only stopped REQUIRING the verb, and the gateway answers it through Funduq.as_reader(the key the socket proved) with its own 'a provider may only read threads for agents it serves' check in front, which is strictly stronger than core's circle for an unbound thread. Full field semantics in docs/server-mode.md.
frames.register_agent_entry_comment: One element of register.agents, and it IS funduq_contract.Registration — extra='forbid', so a misspelt key is a validation error at the door rather than a field silently dropped on the way into core. 'takesInterjections' arrived at contract revision 12: the remote link declares, per agent, whether that agent takes a run addressed at its thread's live run, derived by the SDK from the presence of the interjection hook and never typed by an author. funduq reads it back off the link at registration and writes it onto the agent card as the interjection extension's URI. An entry omitting it behaves exactly as before.
